newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada legislators urge relax foreign bank rules.
newsitem.headline: Canada legislators urge relax foreign bank rules.

text.p: Foreign banks should be given freer access to Canada's banking market, including the option of opening branches to provide more competition to the country's six big banks, Canadian legislators said on Thursday.
Canada should join other industrialized countries in lifting broad restrictions on the way foreign banks operate, said the finance committee of Canada's unelected upper house.
The Senate report goes farther than the federal government's white paper on financial reforms released earlier this year which suggested minor changes to foreign bank rules.

"The committee's proposal to clear the way for foreign banks to carry on wholesale banking activities in Canada will create a more competitive domestic banking environment," the committee's deputy chairman, senator David Angus, said in a statement.
The finance committee of the House of Commons, the country's elected chamber of Parliament, issued a similar report on Thursday.
In recent years, several foreign banks abandoned Canada because of its restrictive banking laws and stiffer than expected competition from the domestic banks.
Under current rules, offshore banks must set up a federally regulated subsidiary with its own capital, board of directors and audit system.

The finance committees proposed allowing foreign banks to compete for business loans under a less regulated branch structure. But offshore banks must still pay their fair share of taxes, including capital taxes.

"While the committee strongly recommends quick access to direct branching, we do not wish to provide foreign banks with an unfair competitive advantage over Canadian banks," the House of Commons finance committee said in its report.

Foreign bankers welcomed the finance committee reports and suggested banks that have shied away from Canada may give the country a second look if the changes are adopted by the federal government in its 1997 review of Canada's Bank Act.

"With greater flexibility in the way they can structure their Canadian operations, foreign banks can be expected to increase their already important role in trade finance, corporate lending, loans syndication and capital markets," Fred Buhler, chief executive officer of BankAmerica Corp's Canadian subsidiary. The number of foreign banks in Canada has dropped from a peak of more than 60 to the 43 today. -- Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100
